H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in Jacobson v. Massachusetts (1905) did not hold that mandatory municipal smallpox vaccination ordinances violate Fourteenth Amendment substantive bodily liberty. In fact, the Court upheld the constitutionality of a Massachusetts statute that authorized local boards of health to require vaccination against smallpox, holding that the police power of a state includes the authority to enact reasonable regulations to protect public health and safety (ID: 197_0011-01). The Court rejected the claim that the vaccination ordinance violated the plaintiff's liberty protected by the Fourteenth Amendment, finding that the ordinance was a reasonable exercise of the state's police power.
